name: atr_expansion_breakout_5s_2
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: When a single 1-min bar's range exceeds 2x the 20-bar ATR, it signals a volatility expansion event — often caused by institutional block trades or news catalyst. These expansion bars tend to have follow-through because the force that caused them (large order, news) persists for 15-30 minutes. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders are either stopped out by the expansion bar or are too scared to enter after it. Not fully arbitraged because distinguishing genuine expansion from noise requires volume confirmation.
mechanism: ATR measures the amplitude of recent price swings. When current price movement exceeds the ATR envelope, it signals a breakout from the volatility regime. Such breakouts typically result from institutional flow entering the market, and the move persists until the flow is absorbed, usually within 1-3 ATR multiples of the breakout point.

exit.signal_exit: exit if 3 consecutive bars move against the expansion direction

filters.volume_filter: expansion bar volume must be > 2x 20-bar average

weaknesses: Entry at expansion bar close means you're chasing. Slippage of 5 bps is optimistic — real fills during fast moves can be 10+ bps.
Expansion bars caused by fat-finger trades or erroneous prints reverse instantly. No way to distinguish from genuine flow in real-time.
Stop at opposite end of expansion bar can be wide (the bar itself is 2x ATR), creating large per-trade risk.
prior_art: Volatility expansion / wide-range bar trading. See: Mark Minervini, Linda Raschke (Holy Grail setup).
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
